article_type: explanatory guide (benefits and limitations) with worked calculation and evidence review
search_intent: Explanation of benefits and limitations with decision support (is Scrum worth it for this work?)
h1: Advantages of Scrum: Benefits, Limitations and Evidence
seo_title: Advantages of Scrum: Benefits, Limitations and Evidence
meta_description: The advantages of Scrum explained: how each benefit arises from the Scrum Guide, the conditions it depends on, what research shows and the limitations.
excerpt: Where each advantage of Scrum comes from, the condition it depends on, what a 1,978-team study found, an illustrative calculation of spend at risk between inspections versus the time cost of the events, and where Scrum fits poorly.
learning_objectives: Explain how each advantage of Scrum arises from a specific element of the 2020 Scrum Guide
Identify the precondition each advantage depends on and the warning sign that it is missing
Calculate maximum spend between inspections and the time cost of Scrum events for a team
Summarise what the Verwijs and Russo (2023) study found and its limitations
Decide whether Scrum's advantages outweigh its costs for a given piece of work

external_references.title: The 2020 Scrum Guide (November 2020), Schwaber and Sutherland
external_references.what_it_supports: Definition of Scrum; Sprints of one month or less; predictability; shorter Sprints limit risk of cost and effort; quality does not decrease; team typically 10 or fewer; purposefully incomplete; makes visible efficacy of management; immutability end note; multiple Increments per Sprint; Sprint Review not a release gate

external_references.title: The 2017 Scrum Guide (PDF)
external_references.what_it_supports: Historical guideline that refinement usually consumes no more than 10% of Development Team capacity

external_references.title: Verwijs, C. and Russo, D. (2023) A Theory of Scrum Team Effectiveness. ACM TOSEM 32(3), Article 74. doi:10.1145/3571849
external_references.what_it_supports: 4,940 respondents, 1,978 teams; effectiveness = stakeholder satisfaction + team morale; five factors; stakeholder concern beta .513 and responsiveness beta .402 direct effects; management support indirect only; stated limitations (cross-sectional, self-report, voluntary sample, software teams)

formulas.formula: E = C x I; share = E / B x 100%
formulas.variables: E maximum spend between inspections (GBP); I interval between stakeholder inspections (weeks)

formulas.formula: Event share = event hours / (hours per week x Sprint weeks) x 100%
formulas.variables: event hours per person per Sprint (h); 37.5 h/week; 2-week Sprint

formulas.formula: Event cost = event hours x people x (cost per week / hours per week)
formulas.result: GBP 7,467 per Sprint; GBP 89,600 over 12 Sprints (13.3% of budget)

formulas.formula: Sprint Goal success rate = Sprints with goal met / Sprints completed x 100%
